links.outcome: LLM triage discordance across prespecified demographic and clinical subgroups versus routine triage
links.effect: Discordance varied by subgroup; lower-acuity assignments were more frequent in older adults, trauma, and diabetes, while infectious presentations showed the highest concordance. Overall lower-/higher-acuity discordance was 9.8% and 18.9%.
links.quote: Discordance varied across subgroups; lower-acuity assignments vs routine triage were more frequent in older adults, trauma, and diabetes, while infectious presentations showed the highest concordance.

links.outcome: Sensitivity of LLM for urgent versus non-urgent ED triage classification
links.effect: Urgent/non-urgent AUC 0.768, sensitivity 0.630, specificity 0.906; lower-acuity discordance 9.8%, higher in older adults, diabetes, and trauma.
links.quote: For urgent/non-urgent classification, AUC was 0.768, sensitivity 0.630, specificity 0.906.

screen.reason: Retrospective evaluation of an LLM for ED triage comparing outputs to routine triage decisions across subgroups, evaluating performance and subgroup discordance without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment intervention.
